h1: The 6 Best Cordless Lawn Edgers for Sharp Garden Borders, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Cordless Lawn Edgers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 cordless lawn edgers from WORX, Garvee, EWORK and VEVOR compared on blade size, 20V battery kits and trench or trimmer design.
summary: The WORX WG163 20V 12 inch 2-in-1 is the cordless edger to buy if you want one tool to trim string and edge, and the Garvee 20V 9 inch with a 4.0Ah battery is the stronger blade edger. The WORX WG898 7 inch trencher is the compact border tool, EWORK includes two batteries, and the VEVOR 8.8 inch blade is a budget alternative.
intro: The word edger covers two different tools. One is a blade edger that cuts a vertical slice along a sidewalk or flower bed, leaving a crisp trench. The other is a string trimmer that you turn on its side, which clips grass but does not cut the soil. People often buy the second and expect the first, then wonder why their edge looks fuzzy. Decide which result you want before you buy.

We reviewed eight listings, set aside a corded 12 amp WORX and a basic 12 inch string trimmer, and ranked six cordless edgers by blade or head size, battery capacity, battery count and how well each suits borders and sidewalks. Listings leave out runtime and cutting depth, and we say so. Price buckets replace exact prices, and nothing here comes from test runs.

products.name: WORX 20V 12" 2-in-1 Cordless String Trimmer & Electric Lawn Edger, WG163
products.verdict: A 20V, 12 inch cordless tool that works as both a string trimmer and a lawn edger.
products.description:
The WORX WG163 is a 20V cordless tool with a 12 inch cutting swath that switches between string trimmer and lawn edger modes, and costs between $100 and $200. It is the most established name in this group.

The 2-in-1 design is a practical answer for small yards: one tool trims the fence line and edges the walk, and the WORX battery system is shared across many tools. It wins because it does both jobs competently and comes from a brand with good parts availability. As an edger it is a string-based tool in edge mode, so the cut is cleaner than from a trimmer on its side but not as deep as a blade.

Buy it if you want one tool for trimming and light edging. Skip it if you want a deep, blade-cut trench.
cons: String edging is not a deep trench
products.idealFor: Small yards needing one tool for trim and edge.
products.skipIf: You want a deep blade-cut trench.

products.name: Garvee 20V 9" Cordless Lawn Edger with 4.0Ah Battery & Charger
products.verdict: A 9 inch blade edger with a 4.0Ah battery and charger included, for $50 to $100.
products.description:
The Garvee is a 20V cordless lawn edger with a 9 inch blade, supplied with a 4.0Ah battery and a charger. It sits between $50 and $100.

The 4.0Ah battery matters because edging is a long, continuous job: you walk the whole border, and a small battery runs out partway. A 4.0Ah pack roughly doubles the run time of a 2.0Ah one. The 9 inch blade is the largest in this guide, which gives a deeper, cleaner cut along a sidewalk. It ranks second because the brand is less established than WORX, and the listing gives no cutting depth.

Buy it if you have a long edge to cut and want a real blade. Check the replacement blade supply before you buy.
pros: Low price for a blade edger

products.name: WORX Cordless Lawn Edger, 20V 7" Trencher for Lawn Border Tending, WG898
products.verdict: A 20V, 7 inch blade trencher from WORX for neat lawn borders.
products.description:
The WORX WG898 is a 20V cordless trencher-style edger with a 7 inch blade, described for lawn border tending, and costs between $100 and $200.

A 7 inch blade is compact and light, which suits a small garden or a user who prefers a tool they can handle easily. Trencher-style edgers cut a vertical slice that defines the lawn edge, and a smaller blade needs less power and weighs less. It ranks third because the blade is smaller than the Garvee's and the listing leaves out the battery capacity.

Buy it if you have a small yard and already own WORX tools. Check whether the battery is included before you order.

products.name: EWORK 20V Cordless Lawn Edger with 2 Batteries & Charger for Lawns Care
products.verdict: A 20V cordless edger supplied with two batteries and a charger.
products.description:
The EWORK is a 20V cordless edger supplied with two batteries and a charger, priced between $100 and $200.

Two batteries are the draw: you can swap a fresh pack in when the first runs low and keep edging, which turns a half-job into a finished one. The listing does not give blade size or battery capacity, so the real run time is unknown. It ranks fourth because those gaps weigh against it, and the brand is less established than WORX.

Buy it if you want a ready-to-go kit with a spare battery. Check the blade diameter and amp-hour rating with the seller first.
pros: Swap packs to finish the job
products.idealFor: Larger yards needing a spare battery.
products.skipIf: You want a stated blade size.

products.name: VEVOR Lawn Edger 8.8-in Blade, 20V Battery Powered Cordless Edger Lawn Tool
products.verdict: An 8.8 inch blade, 20V cordless edger at $100 to $200.
products.description:
The VEVOR lawn edger has an 8.8 inch blade and a 20V battery, and costs between $100 and $200.

The blade is nearly as wide as the Garvee's and wider than the WORX WG898's, which gives a deep, tidy cut. VEVOR is better known for tools than for lawn equipment, so after-sales support is less certain. It ranks fifth because the price is higher than the Garvee's and the listing leaves out battery capacity.

Buy it if you want a wide blade and a lower price than a WORX. Check the battery details before buying.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers wanting a wide blade.

products.name: Cordless Lawn Edger, 20V Battery Powered Edger for Lawns Sidewalk
products.verdict: A generic 20V battery edger for lawns and sidewalks, with almost no detail.
products.description:
This listing is a 20V battery-powered edger for lawns and sidewalks, priced between $100 and $200, with no brand, blade size or battery information.

The sparse detail is why it ranks last, since the other edgers here at least state a blade size or a battery. It may suit a buyer who finds it at a discount, but you cannot judge its power or run time from the page.

Buy it only if the price undercuts the Garvee and the return window is generous. Otherwise choose a model with stated specs.
products.idealFor: Bargain hunters who can return it.

whatMatters.detail: A blade edger cuts a clean vertical trench along a sidewalk or bed. A string tool in edge mode trims the grass but does not cut the soil. Choose a blade if you want a crisp, lasting edge.
A bigger blade, such as 9 inches, cuts deeper but weighs more. A 7 inch blade is light and suits small gardens. Check the diameter in the title.
Edging a long border drains a battery. A 4.0Ah pack lasts about twice as long as a 2.0Ah pack, and a second battery lets you swap and keep working. Listings often omit this, so ask.
You carry the edger along a long edge, so weight matters. A tool that feels front-heavy tires the wrist. Look for adjustable handles or a wheel guide in the description.
Blades dull and need replacing. Check that spares are sold, and wear eye protection and sturdy shoes. Keep the guard in place and clear stones from the path first.

faq.q: Do I need a lawn edger if I have a string trimmer?
faq.a: Not strictly. A trimmer on its side can tidy an edge, but a blade edger cuts a crisp trench that lasts longer. A 2-in-1 like the WORX WG163 covers both for a small yard.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a lawn edger?
faq.a: Ignoring battery capacity. A small battery dies halfway along a long edge. Look for a 4.0Ah pack or a second battery.

faq.q: Is the WORX WG163 worth it over the Garvee?
faq.a: If you want one tool for trimming and edging, yes. If you want a deep, blade-cut border along a sidewalk, the Garvee is the better edger and costs less.
Charge the battery, fit the blade guard and handle, and set the cutting depth if the tool has one. Most take under 15 minutes. Practice on a short stretch first.

faq.q: How do I keep blades sharp?
faq.a: Clean soil off after use, check the blade for nicks and replace it when it dulls. A sharp blade cuts cleaner and drains the battery less.

faq.q: Is edging safe near paths and cars?
faq.a: Stones can fly, so wear eye protection and sturdy shoes, and keep bystanders away. Clear loose debris from the edge before you start.

finalTake: For a small to average yard, the WORX WG163 is the best cordless lawn edger here, with 2-in-1 versatility and a reliable platform. The Garvee 9 inch with a 4.0Ah battery is the best pure blade edger and a bargain, the WORX WG898 suits small gardens, and the EWORK adds a spare battery. Decide between a blade edge and a string edge before you buy.
